what: The discoveries HorizonMath (arXiv 2603.15617v2) credits to frontier models, decided from what its Appendix A prints, by standard-library deciders that share no code with its validators.

rows.problem: Asymptotic Upper Bound Constant for Diagonal Ramsey Numbers (solvability 1)
rows.claim: R(k,k) <= 3.6960839126^(k+o(k)), improving 3.7992 (Gupta–Ndiaye–Norin–Wei), by a certificate that satisfies their Theorem 14
rows.claimant: GPT-5.4 Pro, reproduced by GPT-5.6 Sol Max (HorizonMath, arXiv 2603.15617v2, Appendix A.3)
rows.scope: the certificate is refuted, not the inequality: its pair (X(1), Y(1)) = (0.22745, 0.9988), at the point that sets c, lies outside R — Erdos's 1947 bound at e = 13/2000, p = 11981/500000 exceeds the pair's rate by 0.00130 — and 56 of its 201 decided points are outside R, 128 more not placed in R by the bound the problem names. The problem's own rule accepts every pair with x <= e^-U(1) = 0.26292, whatever y is: it asks one of the two inequalities membership needs

decided.claim: the certificate satisfies GNNW Theorem 14, so R(k,k) <= 3.6960839...^(k+o(k))

checks.name: the problem's rule accepts (X(1), Y(1)): X(1) <= e^-U(1), so -ln X(1) - s ln Y(1) >= U(s) on all of (0, 1]
(X(1), Y(1)) is NOT in R: the Erdos bound excludes the pair the diagonal constant is read at

rows.theirChecker: valid: true — "Valid split certificate; c = e^{F(1)} = 3.69608391263; polynomial_coeffs degree = 5; analytic tail endpoint = 0.00010846; worst small-lambda slack = 0.000272305; worst large R_0 slack = 0.000951234; worst large main slack = 0.000318787"

theirCheckerWithAnd.change: validators/ramsey_asymptotic.py line 299, `return max(mp.mpf(0), min(bu, bs))` -> `max(bu, bs)`: the pair must clear BOTH orientations' thresholds, as membership in R requires

the printed 0.1091479892 is the exact area's truncation or rounding

rows.problem: Fifth Airy moment a5; equal-power TE+TM and non-resonant TM/TE spherical-mode quality factors (solvability 2)
rows.claim: three closed forms that "pass the compliance check and match the high-precision reference"
rows.scope: the expressions are not published: the paper says all six discoveries "are detailed in Appendix A", which details three (A.1–A.3), none of these; agreement with a reference to 20 digits would not decide equality in any case

notDecided.why: the closed form Gamma(1/4)^2/(8 sqrt(pi)) + Gamma(3/4)^2/sqrt(pi) comes with a printed derivation (Landen, then a Beltrami transform, to 2E(1/2) - K(1/2)/2); an enclosure of the integral to hundreds of digits, or a check of each step, is not built here yet
